content.text:
**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The termination architecture already sits at the playbook's preferred position:

| Rule element | Document | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Customer convenience right | §14 — at-will on written notice, ~30–60 days effective | Preferred (30 days) |
| Early-termination fee | None anywhere | Better than fallback cap |
| Vendor convenience right mid-term | None; only cause-based cut-off of §§2–3 | Preferred |
| Term length | 1 year, auto-renewing | Walk-away test (multi-year, no exit) not triggered |

Two sub-elements noted in the rationale rather than flagged, consistent with the classification rules: no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (largely moot, since §5a bills monthly in arrears), and the end-of-term non-renewal notice is 30 rather than 90 days — but that right is mutual, operates only at natural expiry, and tightening it would cut back our own flexibility, so it is not worth a redline.

One open item for confirmation: §14 opens "Subject to Section 4 hereof," and Section 4 was not in the reviewed text. The cross-references in §6 (p0047) suggest Section 4 deals with minimum monthly fees, not termination limits, but I'd confirm that when the full Section 4 is available — if it in fact conditions or restricts Client's termination right, this finding should be revisited.
